The Google effect now has a brain scan.
University College London published it on October 5th, in Scientific Reports.
Volunteers in an fMRI scanner saw faces and scenes, then got one of three cues.
Remember this. Forget this. Or: save it, and a reminder will come later.
The save cue produced brain activity that closely resembled the forget cue.
When people had to remember, the neural trace of the picture persisted.
After save or forget, it faded until it was statistically gone.
The authors suggest it may be adaptive: freeing limited brain space for what matters.
